Hi, A little background, I am 5'6 female who weighted 180 lb at heaviest, I am now 135lb. I reached my goal by simply reducing my caloric intake gym was not in my plans until recently. Now I want to see some muscle growth and definition. Where do I start? What food should I remove or add too my life? What program should follow? I have looked into online forums about this but they only give me general ideas.......I'm confused by the vague suggestions "Eat better, go to the gym and do these wickedly weird exercises" is there a program and a dietary plan I can follow?
Need some suggestions on body building.

Well, don't forget that the reason there are a million diets and a million exercise routines is that, to some degree or another, all of them work. This is because, in the long run, the benefits you're going to get are counting on the fact that your body is a resilient, strong chunk of flesh that's going to be doing its best to be healthy despite everything you screw up with it.

For exercise, I recommend Stronglifts 5x5 as a good starting place. It's focused on functional strength, which is not necessarily the fastest way to "large looking muscles", but it's a great place to start. Working on the form for your exercises will get you more in touch with how your muscles are working and what they're for. Additionally, because these are 'free weight' exercises, you'll build lots of support muscles that you'll never really see--but these are gonna be necessary for you to have big, strong primary muscles that you can actually use.

For diet, I recommend picking up My Fitness Pal and starting off with its "default" diet. You'll probably want to up your protein from what that diet considers 'standard'. Over the various places I go for advice, I've seen people suggest that you should target 1-2 grams of protein per day, per pound of lean muscle mass you hope to have eventually. So, for me with a lean muscle mass of about 200lbs, I'm trying to hit about 350g of protein in a day. At this point, I choose to just accept the extra calories on top of the 'normal' diet that it takes when I throw in all that extra protein, but you could try to balance it back down so your daily calories don't change, if you want.
What ever you will always do. Do that. Can start with push ups, sit ups, body weight squats. Then grow from there.

Make protein a larger part of your diet

This is what muscle is made of. Without enough protein, your body may be like "Dang, I would like to build some muscle so that these exercises we're doing would get easier, but I just don't have the raw materials."

Chicken, tofu, beans, steak, eggs; doesn't matter how.

Bonus: It's usually harder to find unhealthy foods that are good sources of protein.

Continuing to eat healthily and lean will keep your body from hiding your developing muscles underneath a layer of fat. You can be strong, but if you overeat your muscles won't be visible and you won't have that "definition" or "tone."

Use the muscles you want to grow

That's really it. Use them regularly, and use them lots. You're getting enough protein for your body to build some muscle, now you need to indicate to it which muscles to build, and you'll do this by using them.

If you're not trying to do things that are difficult and pushing the envelope of what you're capable of, your body won't really decide that you need to grow more muscle to meet the demands you place on it.

If you don't do it regularly, your body also won't really decide that you need to grow more muscle to meet the demands that you're placing on it, because it's not a regular occurrence and it would be wasteful to bulk up.

Are there some exercises, or sets of exercises, or routines that are provably more effective than others? Almost certainly. But also almost certainly, when starting out, you won't need to try this hard to optimize your exercises; any rigorous routine will work. As time goes on, and you bulk up, and you acquire life experience working out, you will be both in a better position to decide which exercises are optimal for you, and your body will be getting to a point where those choices matter.
